scope: Read-only source, saved-scene and visual-evidence audit for the current Android release. No Assets or Console mutations. Suggested declarations are subject to the exact live questionnaire wording; this is not a compliance certificate or a final age rating.

audience.knownUserInstruction: User explicitly described children aged 4–15 when requesting ability-card design. This is a material child-audience signal and must not be silently replaced by an adult-only target.
audience.repoPlan: PLANS/COGHE_MONETIZATION_PLAN.md sections 0 and 12 leave final publishing audience unresolved. A historical UI brief and the final marketed age range may differ; the owner must resolve that distinction if necessary.
audience.caveat: Do not select these groups mechanically. Confirm that content and interaction design are appropriate for each group, especially preschool users, and resolve the runtime gaps below before asserting readiness. An IARC rating and a declared target audience are different fields.

releaseBlockersOrUnverifiedItems.detail: Unconditional analytics start and identifier permissions require an explicit child/unknown-age policy and verified suppression before SDK collection. No code guard currently supplies that assurance. Do not state that adding an AdMob age flag automatically fixes Firebase.

README/build-validation in this verification folder report native code3 publisher misconfiguration: no form(s) configured. Complete relevant account messages and test first-run/denied/changed choices rather than declaring production consent ready.

Verify clear ad labels, no accidental touch overlap, no simultaneous placements, and dismissal timing for child/unknown users. Existing pacing and opt-in rewarded logic are useful but do not establish Families format compliance.

Ad-gated hidden rewards are present. Review presentation, voluntary skip, no pressure, and exact questionnaire wording; no odds text was seen in the popup. Current gift code is not proof of simulated gambling, and no cash purchase path exists.

releaseBlockersOrUnverifiedItems.detail: Disclose mild scary creature and armed intro imagery accurately. The audit cannot guarantee a particular IARC/PEGI/ESRB age classification or preschool suitability.

changes: Collect neutral age information before any age-sensitive SDK startup; unknown defaults to the protected branch. Keep DOB/age local unless a justified disclosure explicitly requires otherwise.
Set global MobileAds RequestConfiguration before Initialize using installed AgeRestrictedTreatment.Child and MaxAdContentRating.G for protected requests. Do not combine deprecated flags blindly.
Set the UMP underage parameter separately; UMP does not forward it to GMA. Respect country-dependent consent thresholds.
Default analytics and advertising identifier collection off before SDK init, then enable only the reviewed branch/settings. Review Firebase settings independently of AdMob.
Fix UMP account messages and verify protected/older/unknown flows, reinstall, offline, consent revocation, rewarded dismiss and actual network privacy signals. Rebuild the AAB after code changes.
Only after owner confirms this target, use a consistently child-directed configuration. Remove prohibited identifier permissions and disable associated collection; verify all included SDK uses.

If safe ad and analytics behaviour cannot yet be demonstrated, ship an explicitly approved no-ads/no-analytics release variant and adjust Console/privacy declarations to that actual binary. This changes monetization, so do not silently substitute it for the requested build.
Keep content-rating disclosures and visual suitability review even with SDKs removed.

liveIarcViolenceReview.question: Does the game contain inferences, references or depictions of violence, blood or gory images, including violence directed at the player?
liveIarcViolenceReview.helpTextProvidedByConsole: Please note that this section includes all forms of violence or blood, even mild combat action or avoidance of deliberate environmental hazards.
liveIarcViolenceReview.fearRecommendedAnswer: Yes — mild fantasy monster-head transformation with prominent teeth and tongue; no graphic horror or attack.
rationale: Reviewed intro soldier frames hold rifles lowered or across the chest. They do not aim at or fire at a character. Reaction frame shows a recoil/flinch, not injury.
Meteor impact is a blast with no person or animal depicted being harmed.
All first 65 active campaign scenes were checked for the guillotine script GUID: none use it. Historical implementation classes do not establish current gameplay content.

Slick materials, lifts and breakable glass are traversal obstacles. A fall leaves the creature alive; no damage, pain, health loss, injury or death is depicted. The documented deliberate-hazard clause does not itself turn an obstacle without depicted harm into violence.
Current campaign fail calls are boundary escape and exiting before merging. Failure stops motion and changes outcome, without an injury/death animation.
Quantum separation produces two living portions of a liquid creature, which recombine; no blood, wound or harmful attack is represented.
sourceEvidence: Assets/_Game/Venom/Runtime/VenomLevelController.cs:195 — legacy out-of-bounds failure also only marks Lost and disables input
Assets/_Game/Venom/Runtime/COgheBreakableGlass.cs — pane/shard presentation and a fall, no damage/failure call
liveIarcViolenceReview.limits: Recommendation for the current inspected release and exact live question, not a rating certificate. A dedicated weapons-only question should disclose the held rifles. Reassess if weapons are aimed/fired, attacks, injuries, harmful traps or other active scenes are introduced.

submittedIarcOutcome.interpretation: Preserve generated ratings/descriptors as returned, even where a descriptor differs from questionnaire wording. Do not edit questionnaire answers merely to force a lower result.

ageSuitabilityFollowUp.knownAudienceStillApplies: Historic child audience 4–15 remains a material owner instruction until the owner explicitly changes it. Do not silently declare teens/adults to avoid Families requirements.
ageSuitabilityFollowUp.preschoolAssessment: Do not certify current unchanged runtime as suitable for Ages5-and-under. The observed monster head, armed intro, comic belching and multi-step spatial/control demands raise specific preschool suitability concerns.
ageSuitabilityFollowUp.sixToEightAssessment: Requires explicit suitability/usability assessment for these children. Slapstick and collecting can fit, but current regional ratings and puzzle/control complexity warrant review; the audit cannot certify the whole age band.
ageSuitabilityFollowUp.olderChildrenAssessment: A narrower older-child target may better match current puzzle demands, but this is a design recommendation, not an authorized target-audience change or a guarantee of regional age eligibility.
ageSuitabilityFollowUp.ratingVsAudience: IARC ratings vary by region and are distinct from designed target audience. No primary-source rule was found that mechanically converts PEGI7 into one Console age-group selection. Taiwan12 must not be described as universally suitable from age7.
nextOwnerDecision: Keep preschool as intended audience and revise content and interaction design, then reassess accurate ratings and suitability.
Explicitly retarget the current build to older children while retaining Families treatment for included under13 users and complying with applicable regional ratings.
ageSuitabilityFollowUp.policyBoundary: Google guidance says content may not be suitable for particular ages; this audit does not present that guidance as an automatic absolute ban or a legal age ruling.
